chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abu Ja'far, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the alms-tax (zakat) of wealth that the ruler takes, so he said, 'I do not command you to return it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat if the ruler takes it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when the ruling authority (sultan) collects zakat, the payer is not commanded to repeat the payment, indicating that the obligation is considered fulfilled despite the ruler's possession. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on the validity of zakat paid to the state, distinguishing it from cases where the specific recipient or amount is disputed, and underscores the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding the discharge of duty. It serves as a practical legal guideline for believers navigating the intersection of religious obligation and political authority.
